output.title: When date ambiguity stops working
output.body:
This is for the owner of a 1–10-person business who has tried ChatGPT but has not wired AI into a real workflow yet. The question is not whether AI can read a date. It is whether date ambiguity has become a repeatable workflow problem.

If the same pause keeps showing up in one task, you have something concrete to inspect: a missing timezone, mixed date formats, or two systems disagreeing on the same deadline. In a small business, the choice is usually manual checking, hiring someone to watch it, or a bounded automation that standardises dates at entry and flags anything unclear before it spreads. That is a fit check, not a promise.

A practical next step is simple: watch one recurring workflow for a week and count every time date ambiguity forces a stop, a clarification, or a correction. Use your own numbers, not a guess. If the confusion keeps appearing, ask one more question: does this workflow have one authoritative source, or is the date being recreated in email, forms, spreadsheets, and memory?

If your dates start coming from scans or PDFs, stop there; OCR-heavy work is not where this should begin. The goal is a cleaner source of truth, not more cleverness. Very considerate, with enough friction to be useful.
